Recognize the approach

Flash was a multimedia platform, not a visual style.

Look for

  • Scenes instead of ordinary page changes
  • Coordinated movement and sound
  • Custom illustrated or rendered navigation

Your learning goal

Describe the visual decisions before choosing a tool. Then make one small example that uses them deliberately.

Next: Origins

Where it comes from

Flash was a multimedia platform, not a visual style. Its stage, timeline, and scripting encouraged coordinated animation, unusual navigation, sound, and scene-based websites.

Period or influence
Late 1990s–2000s

What to examine

Look at the heading, one control, the image treatment, and the reading order. Explain which decisions establish the style and which make the page usable.

Next: Construction

How to construct it

  1. Storyboard an interaction and prepare separate background, object, label, and effect layers.
  2. Rebuild behavior using HTML, SVG, Canvas, or WebGL as needed. Sequence sound after user interaction and include reduced-motion alternatives.

Small practice task

Storyboard a menu entrance, a selection, and a transition. Describe which objects move in each frame.

Before you expand it

Test the result at its intended size, on a narrow screen, and with keyboard focus. Preserve editable layers and record the source and license of acquired assets.
